title: Making LB NGM Plates
author: Priota Islam
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbbgiijw
materials: Measure all the pre-autoclave reagents and add to the flask (Use a new weighing boat and spatula for each reagent. Also, the cholesterol is kept in the fridge.)
When autoclave is complete, remove the probe flask

steps.title: Prepare Flasks
steps.instruction: Obtain clean, sterile flasks (identified by autoclave tape) from the glass kitchen.

steps.title: Prepare LB NGM Solution
steps.instruction: Add water to the flasks, mix thoroughly, and label with autoclave tape as ‘LB NGM Rm 5020’.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the bottle cap is not screwed completely shut before placing in the autoclave.

steps.title: Set Up Autoclave
steps.instruction: Prepare the autoclave machine for the sterilization cycle.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the probe bottle is the same size as the largest bottle being used and fill it with water.
Place the temperature probe into the probe bottle.
Fill the autoclave with water until it reaches the grill.
Verify that the waste flask is not too full.

steps.title: Sterilize Media
steps.instruction: Run the autoclave cycle to sterilize the LB NGM bottles.

substeps.instruction: Place bottles in the autoclave, ensuring caps are not screwed completely shut.
Allow the cycle to run (approximately 2.5 hours for 1L or larger bottles).

steps.title: Cool and Mix Agar
steps.instruction: Cool the sterilized agar and prepare it for pouring while wearing gloves to prevent burns.

substeps.instruction: Let the agar cool to approximately 55°C (cool enough to hold for a second with a gloved hand).
Mix the agar well, avoiding excessive shaking to prevent air bubbles.

steps.title: Pour Plates
steps.instruction: Pour the warm agar onto the desired sized plates quickly to prevent blocking the tubings.

substeps.instruction: If not pouring immediately, keep the bottle on a waterbath set to 60°C.
